San Juan is home to galleries of naïve-style painters and women's cooperatives. You can visit a textile workshop to see hand weaving and natural-dye techniques, and meet comadronas—midwives who grow medicinal herbs. Local traditions also include farming, fishing, weaving reed mats and producing textiles. During the walk, you will sample coffee at one of the cafés.

You will then cross the lake by boat to Santiago Atitlán, at the foot of Tolimán Volcano. You will visit a Catholic church where Catholic and Maya beliefs come together and pass the town hall, where elders can be seen in traditional clothing. Local canoe building, crafts and work on the lake remain part of everyday life in the town.

## The Diversity of a Ballestas Islands Tour!

Wildlife watching – The islands are home to a wealth of marine life, including sea lions, Humboldt penguins and numerous species of seabirds, such as pelicans and cormorants. They are a paradise for nature lovers. Boat excursion – The main way to explore the Ballestas Islands is by boat, offering striking views of rock formations, caves and natural arches. El Candelabro geoglyph – Before reaching the islands, you will see the mysterious Candelabra geoglyph, an enormous ancient figure carved into a hillside that resembles a candelabrum. Its origin and purpose remain a mystery. Dramatic coastal scenery – The excursion offers breathtaking views of Peru's coastal cliffs, turquoise waters and surrounding desert landscape. A birdwatcher's paradise – The islands are a dream destination for birdwatchers: thousands of seabirds, including rare species, can be seen in their natural habitat.

Early in the morning, you will transfer to Paracas (up to 4 hours), arrive and embark on a boat excursion to the Ballestas Islands. On the way, you can see the Candelabra, a giant figure carved into the sand in the style of the Nazca Lines. On the islands, you will be able to observe sea lions, pelicans, Humboldt penguins and other seabirds. The boat excursion lasts about 2 hours. Return to the hotel. You will then transfer to Pisco Airport (up to 30 minutes). We will begin our flight over the remarkable Ocucaje Valley, where the mountains contain marine fossils dating back 150 million years. The flight continues over the Santa Cruz, Palpa, Viscas and Ingenio valleys, where the Paracas and Nazca cultures developed (800 BC–AD 700). From the air, we will also see the Great Center of the Lines (Cahuachi) and the famous Nazca Lines, including the Monkey, Dog, Condor, Spider, Hummingbird and other figures. The flight lasts 1 hour and 40 minutes. Afterwards, transfer to Paracas (up to 30 minutes). Lunch. Return to Lima in the afternoon.

## Ballestas Islands — the “Galápagos of Peru”: a Wildlife Paradise!

The Ballestas Islands, often called the “Galápagos of Peru,” are a haven for wildlife, where sea lions, penguins and countless seabirds thrive in their natural habitat. As you cruise through crystal-clear waters, the rocky islands and their living ecosystems bring you close to the wonders of nature. The Nazca Lines, etched into the desert sands of southern Peru, remain one of the world's most intriguing mysteries. These enormous geoglyphs, depicting animals, plants and geometric figures, stretch across the arid landscape and are visible only from above. Their purpose and origin continue to fascinate visitors, offering a glimpse into the enigmatic ingenuity of ancient civilizations.

## Baños: A Paradise for Nature Lovers and Thrill-Seekers!

Baños is a paradise for adventure and nature lovers, where waterfalls tumble down mountain slopes and hot springs invite you to relax at the foot of Tungurahua Volcano. Surrounded by dense tropical forests, Baños has a special atmosphere that combines the excitement of adventure with the tranquility of nature. Every moment in Baños offers a chance to experience the natural world, whether you choose a thrilling zipline ride or a leisurely walk to one of its majestic waterfalls.

Set in a lush green valley at the foot of Tungurahua Volcano, Baños is a charming Ecuadorian town known for its natural beauty and wealth of adventures. With cascading waterfalls, therapeutic hot springs and spectacular views, Baños is a paradise for nature lovers and thrill-seekers. It offers an ideal combination of relaxation and adrenaline, from soaking in mineral hot springs to exciting outdoor activities such as rafting and canyoning. Known as the “Gateway to the Amazon,” Baños brings together a subtropical climate, diverse wildlife and scenic trails leading to remarkable natural attractions. Visitors can ride the famous “Swing at the End of the World,” explore the Devil's Cauldron waterfall or simply enjoy the peace of this picturesque town. Baños' location also makes it a wonderful starting point for exploring Ecuador's varied landscapes, from mountain scenery to jungle adventures.

## Baños: A True Paradise for Adventure and Nature Lovers!

## In Baños, Nature Sings an Ancient Song, Calling You to New Discoveries.

The tourist town of Baños lies in a valley of waterfalls and hot springs near Tungurahua Volcano, which rises to 5,016 meters. Baños has a population of 20,000 and sits at an elevation of 1,826 meters, with an average annual temperature of 20°C. The town invites you to unwind amid beautiful natural surroundings and offers family adventures as well as extreme sports, including rafting, rock climbing, canyoning, ziplining, trekking, mountain biking and bungee jumping. On the first day, you will set off from Baños and visit Quilotoa Lake, which lies in a volcanic crater. On the second day, you will take a short excursion and visit the town center, with its pleasant subtropical climate. Later, we will set out to see the waterfalls: Agoyán, Bridal Veil (Manto de la Novia) and Devil's Cauldron (Pailón del Diablo). There will also be an opportunity to ride the famous “Swing at the End of the World” and try a zipline over the Pastaza Canyon (ziplining is not included in the price — USD 15 per person). Stops: the “Swing at the End of the World,” Agoyán Waterfall, a walk along the canyon, Bridal Veil Waterfall with a cable-car ride, Devil's Cauldron Waterfall and a town tour.

After breakfast, we will explore Baños, one of Ecuador's most scenic and popular tourist towns. The town lies at an altitude of 1,826 meters, amid dense tropical forests, waterfalls and thermal springs, at the foot of the majestic Tungurahua Volcano (5,016 m).

Baños is rightly regarded as Ecuador's adventure capital. Spectacular natural scenery, the relaxed atmosphere of a small town and a wide choice of outdoor activities all come together here. This is the starting point for rafting, canyoning, trekking, mountain biking, rock climbing, canopy rides and bungee-jumping routes.

During our sightseeing tour, we will stroll through the charming town center before setting off along the famous “Waterfalls Route.” Along the way, we will see some of the region's most beautiful natural attractions: Agoyán Waterfall, Bridal Veil (Manto de la Novia) and the impressive Devil's Cauldron (Pailón del Diablo), considered one of Ecuador's most spectacular waterfalls.

We will also visit the famous “Swing at the End of the World,” perched on the edge of a mountain slope with stunning panoramic views. If you wish, you can experience the thrill of a canopy ride above the scenic Pastaza River Canyon (optional, USD 15 per person).

In the afternoon, transfer to Riobamba. Check in at the hotel and enjoy a free evening.

Main stops: the center of Baños, the “Swing at the End of the World,” Agoyán Waterfall, a walk along the canyon, Bridal Veil Waterfall with its cable-car crossing, and Devil's Cauldron Waterfall.
